latin.575: Nos non satisfecimus, sed alius, nempe Christus, pro nobis satisfecit. Idemne dici potest de peccato, Nos non peccavimus, sed alius peccavit pro nobis, aut loco nostro?
latin.576: Deinde quaestio, Quando vero demum satisfacimus in Christo satisfactione eius actuali? parum abest quin sit ridicula: innuit enim duplicem satisfactionem, actualem & habitualem; cum tamen non, ut est peccatum aliud actuale ab Adamo commissum, aliud habituale in nos propagatum ac nobis inhaerens, sic ulla sit satisfactio praeter eam quae a Christo loco nostro praestita est.
latin.577: Praeterea propositio quando satisfacimus in Christo, cum propria non sit, eget expositione, & revocanda est ad propriam: alioqui committitur fallacia plurium interrogationum: continet enim has duas quaestiones: 1. Quando Christus satisfecit? 2. Quando nobis Christi satisfactio imputatur? Ad illam respondeo, quando passus est in cruce; Ad hanc, quando credimus in eum.
latin.578: Quod si similiter resolvas quaestionem, Quando peccavimus in Adamo? in has duas, Quando peccavit Adamus? &, Quando imputatur nobis eius peccatum? Facilis erit responsio ad primam, quando manducavit fructum vetitum in paradiso; ad secundam, ut taceam supponi imputationem, cum tamen, ut dici possimus peccasse in Adamo, non sit necessaria imputatio, sufficiat propagatio peccati, respondeo, quando geniti sumus ab Adamo vitiati & corrupti.
latin.579: Quid in eo est absurdi? Nec tamen sic potuit respondere Vir doctus, quippe qui velit peccatum Adami nobis, iam ab eo tempore quo lapsum est Adam, fuisse imputatum.
latin.580: Caeterum quam multa sint inter Christi satisfactionem & Adami peccatum discrimina iam aliquoties observavimus, & ad Rom. 5. 19. observaturi sumus.

pass_a.575: Placeus presses the asymmetry: 'Christ satisfied for us' does not license 'another sinned for us / in our place.' Sin-talk and satisfaction-talk are not interchangeable slogans.
pass_a.576: 'When do we finally satisfy by his actual satisfaction?' nearly mocks itself. It smuggles a second, habitual satisfaction. There is no such twin: only Christ's one satisfaction in our stead—unlike Adam's actual act versus the habitual vice propagated into us.
pass_a.577: The improper phrase 'when we satisfy in Christ' packs two questions: when Christ satisfied, and when that satisfaction is imputed. Answer: on the cross; and when we believe. Else it is the fallacy of many questions.
pass_a.578: Split 'when did we sin in Adam?' the same way: when Adam ate in paradise; and when his sin is 'ours.' Imputation is not required to say we sinned in him—propagation of the vice is enough: when we were born corrupted from him.
pass_a.579: Nothing absurd in that timing. The opponent cannot use it, because he needs Adam's act imputed from the very hour of the fall, before we existed.
pass_a.580: How many lines divide Christ's satisfaction from Adam's sin we have marked before and will mark again at Romans 5:19. Tip before GAR's Pelagian dart.

575: We have not satisfied, but another, namely Christ, has satisfied for us. Can the same be said of sin: We have not sinned, but another has sinned for us, or in our place?
576: Next the question, When then at last do we satisfy in Christ by his actual satisfaction? is not far from ridiculous: for it hints a double satisfaction, actual and habitual; whereas yet not, as there is one actual sin committed by Adam, another habitual propagated into us and inhering in us, so is there any satisfaction besides that which was performed by Christ in our place.
577: Besides, the proposition when we satisfy in Christ, since it is not proper, needs exposition, and is to be recalled to the proper: otherwise the fallacy of many questions is committed: for it contains these two questions: 1. When did Christ satisfy? 2. When is Christ's satisfaction imputed to us? To that I answer, when he suffered on the cross; to this, when we believe in him.
578: But if you similarly resolve the question, When did we sin in Adam? into these two, When did Adam sin? and, When is his sin imputed to us? the answer to the first will be easy, when he ate the forbidden fruit in paradise; to the second, not to say that imputation is supposed, whereas yet, that we may be said to have sinned in Adam, imputation is not necessary, propagation of sin suffices, I answer, when we were begotten of Adam vitiated and corrupted.
579: What absurdity is there in that? And yet the learned man could not so answer, inasmuch as he will have Adam's sin to have been imputed to us already from that time when Adam fell.
580: For the rest, how many discriminations there are between Christ's satisfaction and Adam's sin we have already observed several times, and will observe at Romans 5. 19.
